clue.text: Son abandoned by huge entertainer

indicators.note: the son is left behind by the word for huge, so that letter drops out of it

parts.note: cosmic means vast, on the scale of the universe

explanation.surface: A child is left behind by an enormous performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian or funny performer is called a comic, a noun use of the adjective.

clue.text: New shirt's cut up after business suit

indicators.note: the rest comes after the business abbreviation

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: the rearranged shirt cuts into the word up, splitting it apart
new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: shirt with 's read as 'has'

explanation.surface: A new shirt is altered to go with a business suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' is the wooing a suitor does, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying suit to someone means wooing them, the romantic pursuit of a partner.

clue.text: Stones for road, motorway, and so on

parts.note: M marks a British motorway, as in M1
et al. is short for et alia, and others

explanation.surface: Materials for road, motorway and similar construction.
explanation.definitionFit: Road metal is the broken stone used to make or mend road surfaces.

clue.text: My face is warm

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Someone says their face feels hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial welcome is friendly and heartfelt.

clue.text: Film producer welcomes Oscars getting near

indicators.note: the producer takes in guests, so the other letters go inside that word

parts.note: a maker is one who produces something
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet, so two Oscars are OO

explanation.surface: A movie mogul hosts Academy Award winners as the ceremony approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' just joins the two inserted pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a 1979 James Bond picture starring Roger Moore.

clue.text: Run West maybe having stolen horse

indicators.note: the actress's name has taken the horse inside it

parts.note: Mae West, the American film actress
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A Wild West rustler fleeing on a stolen horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like the frontier; it is Mae West.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business is to be in charge of it.

clue.text: Order one's driver, perhaps, to be courteous

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire
I is one, so one's is I's
a driver ant is one kind of ant

explanation.surface: Telling one's chauffeur to be polite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' looks like a chauffeur; it is the African driver ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing deference or respect, as in bowing, means being respectfully polite.

clue.text: Roll over a pig?

indicators.note: the list is placed over, covering, the letter on both sides

parts.note: a roster is a roll or list of names

explanation.surface: A pig rolling over in the mud.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig raised for roasting whole is sometimes called by the name of its fate; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Hearsay I found in book about surprise guest?

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole build is read backwards
the gossip and I are found inside the gospel name

parts.note: Mark is a book of the New Testament
goss is informal for gossip, hearsay

explanation.surface: A rumour discovered in a book about an unexpected visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A messenger hired to turn up unannounced and deliver a kiss is an unexpected party visitor.

clue.text: Artist needs that material

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
yon is an old word for that, as in yon hill

explanation.surface: A painter needs that fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial silk fabric made from cellulose is a textile.

clue.text: One hides name following unqualified comment

indicators.note: the one-with-name piece comes after the word for unqualified

parts.note: utter means complete, without qualification

indicators.note: the word for one conceals the name abbreviation within it

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice

explanation.surface: Someone conceals a name after an outright remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything said aloud is a spoken remark or statement, so a comment fits.

clue.text: Top marks for one in test

parts.note: A is the top grade, so several of them are As
say means for example, as in 'say, a dog'

explanation.surface: Getting straight As in an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To assay a metal is to test it for purity, a technical sense of trial.

clue.text: Impressive, being a shopper?

definitions.meaning: ... means striking or effective, as in a ... argument
to shop someone is slang for informing on them, so a shopper is a grass and is informing

explanation.surface: Asks whether going to the shops is remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shopper' looks like a customer; in British slang to shop someone is to betray them to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Effective and significant, and also blabbing secrets to the authorities like an informer.

clue.text: Doesn't want, at first, criminal record

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order
only the opening letter of want is used

explanation.surface: A crook's past offences put someone off at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored, leaving DOESNT plus W to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something down in writing is to log or note it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Barter goods — well, as fence

indicators.note: the word for well stands round the other letters like a fence enclosing a field

parts.note: hale means healthy, in good health
G is the abbreviation for good, so goods gives two of them

explanation.surface: Trading stolen goods with a receiver, and doing it well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fence' looks like a dealer in stolen property, which suits 'Barter' and 'goods'; here it means a surrounding barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Bargaining over price is the same activity as bartering.

clue.text: Became violent, carrying hot exhaust

indicators.note: the phrase for became violent carries the letter inside it

parts.note: got rough means turned violent
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A car's hot exhaust made the situation turn nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: To use up all of something, such as savings, is to run through it.

clue.text: Find out about unusual type of radiation

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, or around, the word for unusual
out signals that the letters are disordered, as in 'out of order'

parts.note: rare means uncommon

explanation.surface: Discover something about an uncommon kind of rays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' gives INFD, which 'about' wraps round the rest; 'Find out' looks like one verb meaning discover.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat rays lie just beyond the red end of the visible spectrum, so are named for that.

clue.text: Not the same frogman?

definitions.meaning: differing or departing from one another
a frogman is an underwater swimmer, and a male swimmer is a gentleman, split 5,4

explanation.surface: Asks whether a scuba diver is a different kind of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Paths that split apart become different, and the second reading describes a male underwater swimmer.

clue.text: See boat crossing lake from mountain summit

indicators.note: the boat goes across the lake, so its letters surround the abbreviation

parts.note: a pinnace is a small ship's boat
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: From a peak, someone watches a boat crossing a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed rocky peak or the highest point of something.

clue.text: Inadequate way to mention wheels

parts.note: a path is a way or track

indicators.note: something that wheels turns round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to mention or refer to

explanation.surface: A feeble way of bringing up a car's wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' looks like a car; here it is a verb meaning turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pitifully poor or feeble is woefully insufficient.

clue.text: Locks up our charm

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a mane is a head of long hair, locks

explanation.surface: Captivated, someone locks away their charm.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate someone or make them fall in love is to bewitch them.

clue.text: Like one film that is not shown for sci-fi author

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the abbreviation is not shown, so those letters drop out of the word for film

parts.note: a movie is a film
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Something like a film that never reaches the screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac, author of I, Robot and the Foundation books, was a giant of science fiction.

clue.text: Beer bottles work for party animal

indicators.note: the beer bottles up, holds inside, the other piece

parts.note: stout is a dark beer
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A beer bottled by a hard-drinking reveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually stays out late partying, a British informal term.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink in bottle

definitions.meaning: a distilled liquor such as gin or whisky
bottle is British slang for courage, nerve

explanation.surface: Liquor sold in a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard liquor such as whisky, and courage, which British slang calls bottle.

clue.text: In Paris, this accident in particular?

parts.note: ce is French for this
RTA is a road traffic accident, a British abbreviation

explanation.surface: Asks whether this mishap in Paris was something specific.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as in 'a certain person', the word picks out one particular thing.

clue.text: About to drink up soft drink

indicators.note: to drink is to take in, so the abbreviation holds the other letters

parts.note: ca. is short for circa, about
p is piano in music, soft

explanation.surface: Someone is about to finish a soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a cup of tea, a hot beverage.

clue.text: 1 + 1 put in for a start

indicators.note: the two ones are placed inside the word for 'for a'

parts.note: per means for each, for a, as in a pound per ticket
I is the Roman numeral one
the number written out in words

explanation.surface: A sum, one plus one, entered at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' is a verb here, to launch something new.
explanation.definitionFit: To be first to develop or open up something is to originate or launch it.

clue.text: I may get by once free outside

definitions.text: I may get by once free outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside, around, the multiplication sign
free signals the letters are released into a new order

parts.note: X is the times sign, read 'by' as in 3 by 4

explanation.surface: A released prisoner muses that they will manage now they are free outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges ONCE as ECON, which goes around X.
explanation.definitionFit: A former prisoner, now released, is someone who was once a convict.

clue.text: Form of wealth, one worshipped in Athens

definitions.meaning: as a combining form, this Greek prefix means of wealth, as in plutocracy
the Greek god of the underworld, honoured by the Athenians

explanation.surface: A kind of riches that Athenians revered.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek prefix for riches, and the god of the dead whose name means the wealthy one.

clue.text: Bullet case, handle with care printed externally

indicators.note: the word care appears on the outside, enclosing the other piece

parts.note: to touch something is to handle it

explanation.surface: An ammunition box labelled 'handle with care' on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge, a paper case holding the charge for a firearm, is an old military term.

clue.text: Bad breath or not, initially offensive

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters have gone wrong and are scrambled
only the opening letter of not is taken

explanation.surface: Halitosis or not, it starts out off-putting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something detestable or repugnant is deeply objectionable.

clue.text: Shade of colour that starts to be put on paint container

indicators.note: the starting letters are added on after the container word

parts.note: paint is usually sold in a tin

indicators.note: starts takes the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A shade of colour that begins life as paint in a can.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a tint or hue, related to tincture.
